$comment: Columns that scripts/check-sanitize-coverage.mjs flags as sensitive but that deploy/hostinger/sanitize.sql deliberately keeps. Completeness is the checker's job — it derives the candidate list from prisma/schema.prisma on every run. This file is the half a scan cannot produce: the judgement. A column with no entry here and no UPDATE in sanitize.sql fails the check, which is how a new migration is stopped from quietly adding personal data to a dump labelled 'sanitized'.

Contact.emailValidation: Deliverability status, not an address — the values are 'valid', 'deliverable', 'catch_all'. Matched only because the name contains 'email'. Keeping it lets contact-quality bugs reproduce locally.

Template.subject: Reusable template authored by the tenant's own staff, with merge tokens rather than substituted values. No prospect data, and keeping it is what makes a template-rendering bug reproducible. The per-contact rendering (SequenceStepCopy) IS scrubbed.
Template.body: Template body as authored by the tenant's staff: marketing copy with {{merge}} placeholders, not substituted values. Keeping it is what makes a rendering bug reproducible locally; the per-contact rendering in SequenceStepCopy is scrubbed.

AbTestVariant.subject: A variant of a Template; same reasoning.
AbTestVariant.body: An A/B variant of a Template body, authored by staff and carrying merge placeholders rather than any prospect's data. Scrubbed at the point it is rendered for a contact, not here.

Sequence.description: Staff-authored description of a sequence ('Q4 outbound, SaaS founders'), not about any person.

IcpProfile.description: Staff-authored description of an ideal-customer profile ('Vietnamese manufacturers, 50-500 staff'), which describes a market segment rather than any person. Keeping it is what makes an ICP scoring bug reproducible.
